title: Forensic Evidence Preservation playbook for Private Deploys
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook defines the minimum technical, operational, and legal controls required to preserve tamper-evident forensic artifacts for Redwood private (VPC and on-prem) deployments. It is intended for operator teams executing upgrades, rollback events, or incident investigations where evidence continuity and customer-bound proofs are required.

Scope

- Applies to: private (VPC and on-prem) customer deployments running Redwood runtime and control-plane agents.
- Excludes: hosted API infrastructure, ephemeral CI test clusters.
- Phases covered: pre-upgrade, in-flight upgrade/rollback, post-upgrade validation, and evidence handoff.

Goals

1) Ensure a reproducible chain of custody for telemetry, configuration snapshots, and cryptographic proofs.
2) Minimize customer-impact while preserving artifacts for up to the contractual retention window.
3) Provide operator-safe commands and checklist steps that integrate with existing field tooling and audit flows.

Owner & Contacts

- Primary owner: Security (Private Deployments security liaison)
- Runbook lead (day-to-day): Oncall Operator Team (operator-oncall@redwood.example.com)
- Escalation: Incident Response (pager: IR-Team)

Policy: What must be preserved

Operators must capture and retain the following artifact categories for every upgrade or rollback where evidence preservation is requested (customer-triggered or internal):

1. Runtime binary and image metadata
- Image digest and provenance (sha256).
- Signed manifest (if using image signing).

2. Configuration and policy snapshots
- Operator config (yaml) at time T0, T1 (pre/post), and at rollback points.
- RBAC policies and tenant-level overrides.

3. Telemetry & logs
- Supervisor logs (info+ and above) for the control plane component handling the change.
- Runtime inference logs (sampling) including KV-cache events, model swap events, and failure traces.
- Network capture (pcap) snippets for the control-plane handshake windows if requested and allowed by contract.

4. Cryptographic proofs and attestation
- Signed attestations from the operator appliance / HSM if available.
- KMS operation logs (rotation, unwrap/unwrap events) referencing the change.

5. Audit & chain-of-custody artifacts
- Operator signature (operator id + timestamp).
- Evidence manifest (JSON) listing captured artifacts, checksums, capture commands, and retention TTL.

Retention and SLAs

- Standard retention: 90 days internal retention for medium-severity upgrades; 1 year for regulated customers if contracted.
- Evidence delivery SLA: 5 business days for initiating a preserved evidence bundle; 15 business days for full secure handoff (encrypted archive + verification).

Pre-upgrade checklist (operator)

1) Customer confirmation: obtain explicit customer consent form (ticket/ack) to preserve forensic artifacts and deliverable retention window.
2) Baseline capture: run baseline-capture script (see commands below) and generate evidence-manifest-v1.json.
3) Secure channel: validate secure uplink for evidence (S3 with customer-provided KMS or on-prem encrypted NFS).
4) Quiesce windows: identify low-traffic window, coordinate with customer for short quiesce if network-capture is needed.

Commands: baseline capture (example)

# Run on operator host with access to runtime control-plane
redwood-ops capture-baseline --output /tmp/evidence-bundle 
  --include-images --include-configs --include-logs --snapshot-kv-cache 
  --reason "pre-upgrade snapshot" --operator-id "operator-01"

# Generate signed manifest (requires local HSM/KMS)
redwood-ops sign-manifest --manifest /tmp/evidence-bundle/manifest.json --key-id "hsm-001" --out /tmp/evidence-bundle/manifest.signed.json

Forensic artifact manifest example (evidence-manifest-v1.json)

{
  "bundle_id": "evidence-20260210-operator01",
  "captured_by": "operator-01",
  "captured_at": "2026-02-10T18:22:00Z",
  "artifacts": [
    {"path": "images/runtime:v5@sha256:...", "sha256": "...", "type": "image"},
    {"path": "configs/operator.yaml", "sha256": "...", "type": "config"}
  ]
}

(Operators should ensure the manifest is base64-signed or HSM-signed before transmission.)

In-flight (during upgrade / rollback)

- Maintain live evidence streaming to an immutable append-only store (recommended: object storage with object-lock or WORM support).
- If bandwidth-limited, prioritize metadata, signed manifests, and compressed control-plane logs; defer heavy artifacts (pcap) until post-window.
- Operators must not alter captured artifacts; any transformation (e.g., redaction) requires a documented, signed justification.

Post-upgrade validation & artifact hardening

1) Verification: verify checksums of images, configs and logs against pre-upgrade manifest.
2) Attestation: produce a signed attestation document describing the outcome (success/failure) and link to bundle ID.
3) Immutable archive: move evidence bundle to immutable store and apply retention tags and contract metadata.

Artifact Delivery and Customer Handoff

- Delivery options (choose per contract):
  - Encrypted S3 URL with customer KMS key + signed manifest.
  - Physical media via secure courier (rare; follow supply-chain evidence policy).
  - Direct customer pull from on-prem evidence repository over mTLS-authenticated API.

- Handoff checklist:
  1. Transfer encrypted archive.
  2. Provide manifest and verification instructions (sha256 checksums, signature verification command).
  3. Log the handoff event in customer ticket and evidence ledger.

Chain-of-custody template (text)

- Evidence bundle ID: __________
- Captured by (operator id): __________
- Capture start: __________ UTC
- Capture end: __________ UTC
- Location of bundle: (s3://... or /mnt/evidence/...)
- Signed by (operator): __________
- Transferred to (recipient): __________
- Transfer method: encrypted_s3|api_pull|physical
- Transfer date/time: __________ UTC
- Notes (redactions, truncations, sampling): __________

Forensic artifact catalog (recommended minimum)

| Artifact Type | Format | Minimum fields | Recommended retention | Notes |
|---------------|--------|----------------|-----------------------|-------|
| Image manifest | JSON | image digest, signed_by | 1 year (contracted) | include SBOM if available |
| Control-plane logs | gziped txt | timestamp, component, level, message | 90 days | sample-level: info+; increase to debug for incidents |
| KV cache snapshot | binary | version, sequence, snapshot-id | 90 days | store checksum and associated model version |
| Network capture | pcap | start,end,filter | 30 days | capture only control-plane handshake ranges unless allowed |

Rollback specific considerations

- If rollback is initiated for safety, capture a pre-rollback snapshot identical to pre-upgrade baseline.
- Preserve both the upgrade and rollback manifests; do not overwrite.
- Record operator decision rationale and link to incident/ticket id in manifest.

Legal and privacy constraints

- Always consult the customer contract and data processing agreement prior to collecting payload-level logs or full pcaps.
- Redact or exclude PII by default; if PII is necessary for an investigation, obtain explicit documented consent.

Automation and integration suggestions

- Integrate capture steps into existing CI/CD pipelines as optional pre/post hooks (redwood-ops hook-capture).
- Use object storage with WORM/object-lock and native KMS integration for immutable retention.
- Emit evidence bundle creation events to the centralized audit topic (kafka://audits.evidence) with only metadata (no payload).

Testing this playbook (game day exercise)

1) Quarterly - run a simulated upgrade that produces an evidence bundle and walks through the full handoff.
2) Verify operator playbook timing: baseline capture (<= 15m), signed manifest generation (<= 5m), upload to immutable store (<= 30m for 1GB).
3) Validate verification scripts with intentionally corrupted artifact to ensure failure detection.

Appendix A — Verification commands

# Verify manifest signature (example using openssl)
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature manifest.sig manifest.json

# Verify SHA256 of artifact
sha256sum runtime-image.tar | awk '{print $1}'

Appendix B — Common failure modes and mitigations

- "Missing manifest" — Mitigation: abort upgrade until operator can generate and sign baseline; if impossible, escalate.
- "Storage not available" — Mitigation: fall back to local encrypted staging and schedule re-upload; document temporary location in manifest.
- "PII collected accidentally" — Mitigation: notify legal, quarantine bundle, and redact or obtain consent; follow customer DPA.

Related pages and references

- See upgrade-and-rollback orchestration guide for automated canary flows.
- See onprem packaging handbook for HSM/KMS appliance installation and attestation integration.
